events.title: Express.js initial release
events.summary: TJ Holowaychuk shipped Express 0.0.1 on January 3, 2010 — a minimal Sinatra-style web framework for Node.js.
events.about: Express is the default HTTP layer for Node APIs — routing, middleware, and request/response helpers in a few lines. It sits under NestJS, early Meteor, and countless REST services. Typical use: `app.get('/users', ...)` with JSON middleware, session cookies, and static file serving.

narrative.whyChosen: Express became the de facto Node web framework and defined the middleware pattern for JS servers.
narrative.whyImportant: It made Node practical for HTTP APIs when the runtime was still new and unproven for production.
narrative.problemSolved: Raw Node HTTP required boilerplate for every route; teams needed a thin, composable router on top.

events.title: npm first released
events.summary: Isaac Schlueter released npm 1.0 on January 12, 2010 — the default package manager for Node.js and the largest software registry on the web.
events.about: npm installs libraries with `npm install express`, publishes packages to the registry, and locks versions in `package-lock.json`. It shaped how JavaScript shares code — from lodash to React to corporate private registries. Every Node project, frontend bundler, and CI install step depends on it.

narrative.whyChosen: npm turned Node from a runtime into an ecosystem with millions of reusable packages.
narrative.whyImportant: It established semver, dependency trees, and publish workflows for modern JavaScript development.
narrative.problemSolved: Node had no standard way to discover, version, and install third-party modules.

events.title: iPad introduced
events.summary: Steve Jobs introduced the iPad on January 27, 2010 — a tablet-sized iOS device between smartphone and laptop.
events.about: The iPad brought touch-first apps to a 10-inch screen — magazines, games, point-of-sale, and field tools. Developers adapted responsive layouts and later split-view multitasking; the 'tablet class' of UX influenced Android tablets and hybrid 2-in-1s. It redefined casual computing for millions who never bought a PC.

narrative.whyChosen: The iPad created the modern tablet category and a new form factor for app developers.
narrative.whyImportant: It expanded mobile development beyond phones into touch-first tablet experiences.
narrative.problemSolved: Users wanted internet and media consumption without carrying a laptop or squinting at a phone.

events.title: Apple A4 chip introduced
events.summary: Apple introduced the A4 system-on-chip on January 27, 2010 alongside the iPad — Apple's first in-house-designed mobile processor.
events.about: The A4 combined an ARM Cortex-A8 CPU with PowerVR graphics in a package Apple designed — not just rebranded Samsung silicon. It shipped in the iPad and iPhone 4, starting Apple's vertical integration of mobile chip design. Every A-series and M-series chip since traces to this SoC strategy.

narrative.whyChosen: The A4 was Apple's first custom SoC — the start of in-house mobile silicon.
narrative.whyImportant: It let Apple tune CPU, GPU, and power together for iOS devices instead of relying on off-the-shelf chips.
narrative.problemSolved: Apple needed tighter control over performance and battery life than merchant ARM chips provided.
